chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Jibra'il (peace be upon him) came to me and said: 'We, the assembly of Angels, do not enter a house in which is a dog, nor a statue of a body, nor a vessel in which is urine.'.
ai.seo_question: What items prevent angels from entering a house according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual criteria for angelic presence, linking physical domestic elements to divine grace. It underscores the Shia emphasis on *taharah* (purity) not just as ritual cleanliness but as a holistic state inviting the angels, while also noting the specific exclusion of dogs and statues as symbols of impurity or idolatry. The mention of vessels used for urine reflects the practical hygiene standards integrated into religious observance in early Islamic society.
